Zionism: Jewish nationalist movement. The arrival of Zionist settlers in Palestine during this period is widely seen as marking the start of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict.
Which of these people was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
David L. Hill is a physicist.
Who among these is a chemist?
Dmitri Mendeleev is a chemist. The synthetic element mendelevium is named in his honor.
What is the atomic number of Livermorium?
Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
What is the atomic number of Polonium?
Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84.
In what year did Alan Turing die?
Alan Turing: Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
In what year was Magnesium discovered?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
Adenosine: Pfizer. Adenosine (symbol A) is an organic compound that occurs widely in nature in the form of diverse derivatives.
Which country is HAL Tejas from?
HAL Tejas: India. The aircraft made its first flight in 2001 and entered into service with the IAF in 2015.
Who is credited with discovering Grus?
Grus (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Grus (or colloquially) is a constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Reynolds number?
Reynolds number: Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet. At low Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be dominated by laminar (sheet-like) flow, while at high Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be turbulent.
Who is credited with discovering Ceres?
Ceres (dwarf planet): Giuseppe Piazzi. Ceres is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
This localized collection of pus builds up within body tissue, usually from bacterial infection, causing redness, pain, warmth, and swelling. What is it?
Abscess is a collection of pus that has built up within the tissue of the body, usually caused by bacterial infection.
First described by Othniel C. Marsh in 1877, this late Jurassic theropod's name means 'different lizard,' a nod to its unusually lightweight vertebrae — what dinosaur is it?
Allosaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived 155 to 143 million years ago during the late Jurassic period (latest Oxfordian to latest Tithonian ages).

Named in 1835 from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue,' these pH-shifting pigments paint blueberries, black rice, and some autumn leaves anything from red to purple to nearly black — what are they?

Anthocyanin (from Ancient Greek (nthos) 'flower' and / (kuneos/kuanos) 'dark blue'), also called anthocyans, are water-soluble vacuolar pigments that, depending on their pH, may appear red, pink, purple, blue, or black.
First described in 1740, this flowering-plant family rivals only the orchid family in sheer number of species, with over 32,000 recognized today — what family is it?
Asteraceae is a large family of flowering plants that consists of over 32,000 known species in over 1,900 genera within the order Asterales.

This fluid-dynamics rule holds that a fluid's pressure drops as its speed increases; the Swiss physicist credited with it published the idea in 1738, though Leonhard Euler derived the actual equation — what's it called?
Bernoulli's principle is a key concept in fluid dynamics that relates pressure, speed and height.
This incurable, always-fatal disease of cattle causes abnormal behavior and trouble walking, with symptoms that may take four to five years to appear after infection — what is this disorder called?
Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly known as mad cow disease, is an incurable and always fatal neurodegenerative disease of cattle.

One species in this genus of flowering shrubs, native to southern China and Indochina, has its leaves processed into the world's tea, while thousands of ornamental cultivars exist for the garden. Name the genus?
Camellia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Theaceae.
Taken by mouth with effects lasting about a day, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever, hives, and dermatitis with less drowsiness than older allergy medications — what is it?
Cetirizine is a second-generation peripherally selective antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), dermatitis, urticaria (hives), and runny nose.
Its Latin genus name literally means three-leaf, and this herbaceous legume, native to Europe, now grows worldwide in around 300 species — what plant is it?
Clover are plants of the genus Trifolium (from Latin tres 'three' and folium 'leaf').

This cosmopolitan bird family includes crows, ravens, magpies, and jays, and its roughly 135 species are known for remarkable intelligence, including self-awareness demonstrated in mirror tests — what's the family?
Corvidae is a cosmopolitan family of oscine passerine birds that contains the crows, ravens, rooks, magpies, jackdaws, jays, treepies, choughs, and nutcrackers.

First patented in Germany in 1920, then independently synthesized by an American chemist in 1932 and marketed in German-speaking Europe as Permonid for its fast onset and short duration, what is this semi-synthetic opioid?
Desomorphine (or in some formulations known as Krokodil) is a semi-synthetic opioid commercialized by Roche, with powerful, fast-acting effects, such as sedation and analgesia.
Along with the platypus, this quill-covered Australian and New Guinean mammal is one of only two living egg-laying mammal groups, and its young are adorably called puggles — what is it?
Echidna are quill-covered monotremes (egg-laying mammals) belonging to the family Tachyglossidae, living in Australia and New Guinea.
This taxonomic family groups hedgehogs of Eurasia and Africa together with the furrier moonrats of Southeast Asia, and takes its name from the Latin for 'hedgehog' — what family is it?
Erinaceidae (from Latin erinaceus, "hedgehog") is a family in the order Eulipotyphla, consisting of the hedgehogs and moonrats.
This field of study, related to economics and business administration, is typically divided into personal, corporate, and public branches. What field is it?
Finance refers to monetary resources as well as the discipline that studies such resources, with related concepts such as money, currency, assets and liabilities.
Testimony at Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán's 2018 trial revealed suitcases stuffed with $3 million in bribes paid to this former Mexican security chief — who is he?
Genaro García Luna (born 10 July 1968) is a Mexican former government official and convicted drug trafficker.
This Italian-American motorsport boss ran a Formula One team for seven years before becoming CEO and owner of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner (born 7 April 1965) is an Italian and American motorsport engineer and former team manager.
This seasonal state of low body temperature, slow breathing, and reduced metabolism helps some animals pass through winter months — what is it?
Hibernation is a state of minimal activity and metabolic reduction entered by some animal species.
First appearing in the fossil record in Egypt some 37 million years ago, this order of small African herbivores once rivaled odd-toed ungulates in size and diversity — which order?
Hyracoidea is a taxonomic order of mammals.

This English independent scientist invented the electron capture detector, was first to spot CFCs spread through the atmosphere, and proposed that the Earth behaves as one self-regulating system. Who was he?
James Lovelock (26 July 1919 - 26 July 2022) was an English independent scientist, environmentalist and futurist.
This Soviet-designed naval helicopter has spawned variants for assault transport, export, and civilian use, and still flies today from Russia to India -- which aircraft?

Kamov Ka-27 (NATO reporting name 'Helix') is a military helicopter developed for the Soviet Navy, and as of 2024 is in service in various countries including Russia, Ukraine, Vietnam, China, South Korea, and India.

A hybrid of the citron and the bitter orange believed to have originated in northeastern India around the 1st millennium BC, this small evergreen citrus tree bears a tart yellow fruit used worldwide — name the fruit?
Lemon (Citrus limon) is a species of small evergreen tree in the Citrus genus of the flowering plant family Rutaceae.
Dubbed the 'Queen of QVC' for her long-running shopping show and holding over 120 patents, this American entrepreneur is also an investor on the reality series Shark Tank — who is she?
Lori Greiner is an American television personality and entrepreneur.

This Milanese thinker was the first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed a mathematics professor — though she spent her final decades on theology and serving the poor. Who was she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi (16 May 1718 - 9 January 1799) was a Milanese mathematician, philosopher, theologian, and humanitarian.

Named from Greek words meaning 'small head,' this congenital condition involves a smaller-than-normal head and can affect brain development, intellectual ability, and motor function — which disorder is it?
Microcephaly (from Neo-Latin microcephalia, from Ancient Greek mikrs "small" and kephal "head") is a medical condition involving a smaller-than-normal head.
Named for the strong odor males emit during rut to attract mates, this thick-coated Arctic hoofed mammal is called 'the bearded one' in Inuktitut — what's the species?
Muskox (Ovibos moschatus) is a hoofed mammal of the family Bovidae.
First isolated by Scottish physician Daniel Rutherford, which group-15 nonmetal with atomic number 7 is the most abundant species in Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
The heaviest living bird, this flightless African species can sprint at 70 km/h and lays the largest eggs of any land animal on Earth — what bird is it?

A Chinese singer famous for annual appearances on a widely watched Lunar New Year television gala, she has served as her country's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?

Peng Liyuan (pinyin: Png Lyun; born 20 November 1962) is a Chinese singer who has served as the First Lady of China since 2012, as the wife of Xi Jinping, the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and paramount leader of China.
The sole genus in its plant subfamily, this evergreen conifer bears needle-like leaves in bunches of two to five and carries its seeds on woody cones — name the tree?
Pine is any conifer in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae.

This oral glucocorticoid medication suppresses the immune system and reduces inflammation in conditions like asthma and COPD, though long-term use risks side effects such as cataracts and bone loss — what's the drug called?
Prednisone is a glucocorticoid medication mostly used to suppress the immune system and decrease inflammation in conditions such as asthma, COPD, and rheumatologic diseases.
Element 88 on the periodic table, this silvery-white alkaline earth metal turns black when exposed to air and glows via radioluminescence as it radioactively decays — which element?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.

Usually hidden below the soil surface but sometimes growing aerial or aerating instead, these plant organs anchor a plant while drawing in the water and nutrients it needs to grow taller and faster — name them?
Root are the organs of a plant that are modified to provide anchorage for the plant and take in water and nutrients into the plant body, which allows plants to grow taller and faster.

Native to the North Pacific coasts, this marine mammal is the heaviest member of the weasel family yet one of the smallest marine mammals, insulated by the densest fur coat in the animal kingdom — what is it?
Sea otter (Enhydra lutris) is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.
Commonly but inaccurately nicknamed for a big cat it wasn't closely related to, this extinct genus of saber-toothed predator roamed the Americas until as recently as 8,200 years ago — which genus?
Smilodon is a genus of extinct felids. It is one of the best-known saber-toothed predators and prehistoric mammals.

Starting with fever and flu-like symptoms before the skin blisters and peels into painful raw patches, this severe drug-triggered skin reaction sits on the same disease spectrum as toxic epidermal necrolysis, only less severe — which condition?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a type of severe skin reaction.

Tucked beneath the lateral fissure of the brain and named for its position near the head's temples, this region handles language comprehension, memory, and emotion — which part of the cerebral cortex?
Temporal lobe is one of the four major lobes of the cerebral cortex in the brain of mammals.
These brightly colored Neotropical birds are known for their oversized, vividly patterned bills, and their chicks hatch completely naked with no down feathers at all — what bird is it?
Toucan are Neotropical birds in the family Ramphastidae.
This member of the herpesvirus family causes chickenpox in children and, upon reactivation later in life, shingles in adults — what is it called?
Varicella zoster virus (VZV), also known as human herpesvirus 3 (HHV-3, HHV3), is one of nine known herpes viruses that can infect humans.
This broad category of limbless, tube-bodied animals ranges from microscopic creatures to a marine species measured at nearly 58 meters long — the longest animal on Earth — what are they called?
Worm are many different distantly related bilateral animals that typically have a long cylindrical tube-like body, no limbs, and usually no eyes.
This mucolytic drug is the go-to antidote for acetaminophen overdose, working by boosting glutathione to neutralize the drug's toxic byproducts — what is it?
Acetylcysteine: Medication used to treat overdose of paracetamol.
Twice President of the Swiss Confederation, this Social Democratic politician left the Federal Council in 2023 to become Secretary General of the Council of Europe — who is he?
Alain Berset: Swiss Federal Councillor from 2012 to 2023.
Nicknamed the boto for its rosy pink hue (especially in males), this South American toothed whale is the largest species of its kind found in a freshwater habitat — what is it?
Amazon river dolphin: Species of toothed whale. The position of the Araguaian river dolphin (I. araguaiaensis) within the clade is still unclear.
This American anthropologist studied women's weaving and blacksmithing work in Indonesia and later designed microcredit programs to fight rural poverty — who was she?
This pigmented ring of skin around the nipple contains sebaceous glands as well as the openings of the milk ducts — what's it called?
Areola: Pigmented area on the breast around the nipple.
The famous AL 288-1 skeleton nicknamed 'Lucy,' unearthed in Ethiopia's Afar region, belongs to which extinct East African hominin species that lived roughly 3.9 to 2.9 million years ago?
Australopithecus afarensis: Extinct hominid from the Pliocene of East Africa.
This inflammatory condition causes recurring, painful mouth sores along with eye inflammation and arthritis, and is diagnosed after at least three sore outbreaks in a year — which condition?
Behçet's disease: Inflammatory disorder. Behçet's disease or Behçet's syndrome (BD; sometimes written Behcet) is a type of inflammatory disorder which affects multiple parts of the body.
Rich in vitamin C and polyphenols, this deciduous shrub's glossy dark berries are cooked into jams and syrups or fermented into cassis — what is it?
Blackcurrant: Species of flowering plant in the gooseberry family Grossulariaceae.

This infraorder of decapod crustaceans tucks a stubby tail-like abdomen under a hard shell and ends its front pair of legs in pincers — over 1.5 million tonnes of them are eaten by humans yearly. What group is it?
Brachyura: Crustacean. The true crabs are the largest of the crab decapod groups with carcinised body forms.
A cole crop related to broccoli, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts, the heaviest recorded head of this leafy vegetable weighed nearly 138 pounds — what is it?
Cabbage: Leafy vegetable in the flowering plant family Brassicaceae.
This infraorder of decapod crustaceans is the true taxonomic home of what everyone actually calls a shrimp, found in fresh and salt water worldwide — what is it?
The largest part of the brain, this structure houses the cerebral cortex plus the hippocampus and basal ganglia, and works with the cerebellum to control every voluntary action. What is it?
Cerebrum: Large part of the brain containing the cerebral cortex.
Selected from over 11,000 applicants for NASA's Teacher in Space Project, this Concord, New Hampshire educator died aboard the Challenger in 1986 — who was she?
Christa McAuliffe: American teacher and astronaut (1948–1986)
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy, this opiate is a prodrug of morphine often paired with paracetamol to treat mild pain, coughs, and even diarrhea — what is it?
Codeine: Opiate and prodrug of morphine used to treat pain. It usually starts working after half an hour, with maximum effect at two hours.
Caused by a fungus that forms galls on maize plants, this disease produces an edible delicacy in Mexico known as huitlacoche, often stuffed into quesadillas — which condition?
Corn smut: Fungal plant disease on maize and teosinte.
Also called Bermuda grass, this hardy warm-climate turf species is ironically not native to the island of the same name — which plant, by its scientific name?
Cynodon dactylon: Species of grass. Cynodon dactylon, commonly known as Bermuda grass or as couch grass in Australia and New Zealand, is a grass found worldwide in warm and tropical climates.
This central nervous system stimulant is the 'right-handed' mirror-image form of a well-known molecule, prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy and sometimes given as an inactive prodrug — what is it?
Dextroamphetamine: CNS stimulant and isomer of amphetamine.
A broad-spectrum member of the tetracycline class, this antibiotic treats everything from acne and chlamydia to Lyme disease and cholera — though it'll make you sunburn more easily. Which drug?
Doxycycline: Tetracycline-class antibiotic. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
Despite its name, this South American freshwater fish is actually a knifefish, not a true eel, and produces powerful discharges using specialized tissue — which species?
Electrophorus electricus: South American electric fish. It is considered as a freshwater teleost which contains an electrogenic tissue that produces electric discharges.
This flowering shrub in the family Erythroxylaceae is one of only two species whose leaves are cultivated to produce a notorious stimulant — which plant is it?
Erythroxylum coca: Species of flowering plant.
Sporting an orange-red breast rimmed in grey and brown upperparts, this small insect-eating songbird ranges from Western Siberia to North Africa — which bird?
European robin: Species of bird. It is found across Europe, as far east as Western Siberia, and as far south as North Africa.

Boldly patterned in black and yellow to warn predators of its toxicity, this European amphibian can live for more than 50 years and is now vulnerable due to an introduced fungal disease — what species is it?
Fire salamander: Species of amphibian. The fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) is a common species of salamander found in Europe.
Traditionally pounded from cassava, plantains, and cocoyam, this West African staple gets a shoutout in Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart — what dish is it?
Fufu: Dough-like food in African cuisine.
The largest of its family, this mostly solitary mammal uses long foreclaws to dig into nests and a sticky tongue to slurp up ants and termites — what animal is it?
Giant anteater: Species of mammal. The giant anteater (Myrmecophaga tridactyla) is an insectivorous mammal native to Central and South America.
One of China's 'Four Great Domestic Fish,' this herbivorous freshwater species was later introduced to Europe and the US to control aquatic weeds — which fish?
Grass carp: Species of fish. This Asian carp is the only species of the genus Ctenopharyngodon.

This prehensile, multi-fingered body part sits at the end of primates' forelimbs — koalas famously have two opposable thumbs on each one, while raccoons are often said to have them despite lacking true opposable thumbs. What is it?
Hand: Extremity at the end of an arm or forelimb.

First synthesized in 1940 by chemist Roger Adams via hydrogenation of THC isomers, this psychoactive cannabis-derived compound is sold in vaporizers despite never being drug-approved — which compound?
Lightest and most abundant element in the universe, it makes up about 75% of all normal matter and fuels the stars — colorless, odorless, and highly combustible. What element is it?
Hydrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 1 (H)
Equal to one-twelfth of a foot and derived from the Roman word for 'twelfth,' this unit of length has been pegged to exactly 25.4 millimeters since the mid-20th century — what is it?
Inch: Unit of length. The inch (symbol: in or ″) is a unit of length in the British Imperial and the United States customary systems of measurement.
Appointed FBI director by Barack Obama in 2013, this former federal prosecutor was fired from the post in 2017 — who is he?
Back in 1859, this Irish physicist proved the link between atmospheric CO2 and what we now call the greenhouse effect — who was he?
A pastor's son and theoretical physicist, this man passed Manhattan Project secrets to the Soviets, served nine years in a British prison, then resumed his science career in East Germany. Who is he?
Klaus Fuchs: German-born British physicist and atomic spy (1911–1988)
Formulated in 1834, this principle of electromagnetism states that an induced current always flows in a direction that opposes the very change in magnetic field that created it — which principle?
Lenz's law: Electromagnetic opposition to change.
Nicknamed "Connie" and instantly recognizable by its triple tail and dolphin-shaped fuselage, which four-engined airliner was the first civil aircraft family to widely use a pressurized cabin?
Lockheed Constellation: Family of US airliners with 4 piston engines, 1943.
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, and the quokka among its 63 recognized species — what is it?
Macropodidae: Family of marsupial mammals. Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.
A Zainichi Korean entrepreneur, this founder and CEO of SoftBank turned a $20 million bet on Alibaba in 2000 into a stake worth around $75 billion — who is he?
Developed in 1955 and later sold under the brand name Dianabol, this anabolic steroid was once widely used for physique and performance enhancement — what is it?
Metandienone: Androgen and anabolic steroid. It is also used non-medically for physique- and performance-enhancing purposes.
Normally equal to 60 seconds, which unit of time has occasionally run 61 seconds long in UTC due to leap seconds, though a 59-second version has never actually occurred?
Minute: Unit of time equal to 60 seconds. The prime symbol ′ is also sometimes used informally to denote minutes.
Also known as green gram, this legume is a staple ingredient across East, Southeast, and South Asian cuisine in both savory and sweet dishes — what is it?
Discovered in 1885 by Carl Auer von Welsbach, this rare-earth element tarnishes quickly in air and produces pink, purple, and yellow compounds when oxidized — which element, atomic number 60?
Neodymium: Chemical element with atomic number 60 (Nd)

A French apothecary and physician who studied at Avignon until the plague closed it, he's far better remembered for 942 cryptic quatrains said to foretell the future — by what Latinised name is he known?
Nostradamus: French apothecary, astrologer and seer (1503–1566)
Common in adolescents during growth spurts, this condition causes a painful bump just below the knee from inflammation where the patellar ligament attaches to the shinbone — what is it?

Osgood–Schlatter disease: Inflammation of the patellar ligament. Osgood–Schlatter disease (OSD) is inflammation of the patellar ligament at the tibial tuberosity (apophysitis) usually affecting adolescents during growth spurts.
This cream-skinned root vegetable, a cousin of the carrot and parsley, actually grows sweeter in flavor after a winter frost — what is it?
Parsnip: Root vegetable in the flowering plant family Apiaceae.
Known online by the alias 'brokep,' this Swedish-born entrepreneur co-founded a famous BitTorrent search engine before launching the privacy-focused registrar Njalla in 2017 — who is he?
Peter Sunde: Swedish entrepreneur and politician. Peter Sunde Kolmisoppi (born 13 September 1978), alias brokep, is a Swedish-born Finnish-Norwegian entrepreneur and politician.
Also called threadworm in the UK and seatworm elsewhere, this common intestinal roundworm spreads via the faecal-oral route and is especially prevalent among children — what parasite is it?
A purplish-black crystalline salt that dissolves into an intensely pink-to-purple solution, this strong oxidizer also appears on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines for wound care — what is it?
The earliest vertebrates known to achieve powered flight, these warm-blooded Mesozoic reptiles had wings stretched from ankle to a dramatically lengthened fourth finger — what were they called?
Pterosaur: Extinct order of flying reptiles.

A pioneer in optical character recognition and speech synthesis, this futurist inventor received the National Medal of Technology from President Clinton in 1999 for his outlook on AI and life extension — who is he?
Ray Kurzweil: American computer scientist, author and futurist (born 1948)
Often called the first modern chemist, which 17th-century Anglo-Irish natural philosopher described the inverse relationship between a gas's pressure and volume in a law that bears his name?
Named for the genus of the Atlantic salmon, this family of cold-water fish also includes trout, char, and grayling — what family is it?
People with this anxiety disorder are fully capable of speech but fall silent in specific situations or around specific people, even when staying quiet brings shame or punishment — what is it called?
Selective mutism: Anxiety disorder blocking speech. Selective mutism usually co-exists with social anxiety disorder.
The only species in its genus, this cosmopolitan pelagic fish from the mackerel family can grow past a metre long and matters hugely to global fisheries — which species?
Skipjack tuna: Species of fish. The skipjack tuna (Katsuwonus pelamis) is a perciform fish in the tuna family, Scombridae, and is the only member of the genus Katsuwonus.

Once meaning a Christian life oriented toward the Holy Spirit, this concept broadened over centuries to describe a subjective sense of the sacred and 'the deepest values and meanings by which people live,' often apart from organized religion. What's the term?
The first variable-sweep-wing aircraft to enter Soviet service, this fighter-bomber was produced from 1967 to 1990 and exported in variants flown across the Arab world — which jet?
Sukhoi Su-17: Soviet variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber. The Sukhoi Su-17 (Russian: Су-17; NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
Also known as estragon, this perennial herb in the daisy family comes in a French variety prized for cooking and a milder Russian variety — which herb?
Tarragon: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae.
After dropping out of Stuyvesant High School and serving in the Korean War, this economist went on to earn a PhD from Chicago and a National Humanities Medal in 2002?
Co-founder and former CEO of a ride-hailing giant, this businessman resigned in 2017 amid allegations he ignored harassment reports, later selling most of his shares for $2.5 billion — who is he?
Travis Kalanick: American entrepreneur and former CEO of Uber.
Colorless, odorless, and practically non-toxic, this organic compound is the main nitrogen-bearing substance in mammal urine — fittingly, its name traces back to the Greek word for urine. What is it?
Urea: Organic compound. Urea, also called carbamide (because it is a diamide of carbonic acid), is an organic compound with chemical formula CO(NH2)2.
Sold under the brand names Trintellix and Brintellix, this antidepressant belongs to a drug class called serotonin modulators and stimulators — which medication?
Vortioxetine: Serotonin modulator antidepressant. Its effectiveness is viewed as similar to that of other antidepressants.

Ranging from microscopic to a record-breaking 58 meters long for one bootlace-shaped marine species, these limbless, usually eyeless invertebrates gave their name from the Old English 'wyrm' — what are they?
What is the chemical symbol for cobalt?
The symbol for cobalt is Co. Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
The symbol for californium is Cf. Californium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cf and atomic number 98.

In what year was Sigourney Weaver born?
Sigourney Weaver: Susan Alexandra "Sigourney" Weaver ( sig-OR-nee; born October 8, 1949) is an American actress.
In what year was Michael Keaton born?
Michael Keaton: Michael John Douglas (born September 5, 1951), known professionally as Michael Keaton, is an American actor.
In what year was Eva Mendes born?
Eva Mendes: Eva de la Caridad Méndez (Spanish: [ˈeβa ðe la kaɾiˈðað ˈmendes]; born March 5, 1974), known professionally as Eva Mendes, is an American former actress.
In what year was Zooey Deschanel born?
Zooey Deschanel: Zooey Claire Deschanel (born January 17, 1980) is an American actress and singer.
In what year was David Tennant born?
David Tennant: David John Tennant (né McDonald; born 18 April 1971) is a Scottish actor.
In what year was Linda Cardellini born?
Linda Cardellini: Linda Edna Cardellini (born June 25, 1975) is an American actress.
In what year was Scott Adkins born?
Scott Adkins: Scott Edward Adkins (born 17 June 1976) is an English actor and martial artist.

Kevin Bacon: Kevin Norwood Bacon (born July 8, 1958) is an American actor.

Song Kang (Korean: 송강; born April 23, 1994) is a South Korean actor.
In what year was Patrick Swayze born?
